sections.content: Absentee owner properties are one of the most reliable sources of off-market deals in real estate. These are properties where the owner lives somewhere other than the property itself — think landlords who are tired of managing rentals, inherited properties sitting vacant, or out-of-state owners who have lost touch with their investment. If you want to find motivated sellers before other investors do, learning how to find absentee owner properties for investing is a skill that can transform your deal pipeline. This guide covers exactly where to find these leads, how to filter for the best opportunities, and how to turn a simple list into closed deals. For a broader look at sourcing motivated sellers across all categories, check out our [How to Find Motivated Sellers: Complete Guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/finding-motivated-sellers).
Why Absentee Owner Properties Are a Goldmine for Investors

Absentee owners are often dealing with problems they can't solve from a distance. A landlord in California who owns a rental in Memphis may be tired of chasing late rent, dealing with maintenance calls at odd hours, or watching property taxes eat into thin margins. An heir who inherited a house in Detroit may just want it gone. These situations create highly motivated sellers — people who will often accept below-market offers just to move on. Studies show that off-market deals can be purchased at 10% to 30% below market value when sellers are truly motivated, and absentee owners frequently fall into that category. If you're just getting started, our guide on [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) is a great place to build your foundation before diving into lead sourcing.
"The best deals are rarely listed on the MLS. They're sitting in county records, tax databases, and skip-trace lists, waiting for the investor who knows where to look."
Where to Find Absentee Owner Property Lists
1. County Assessor and Tax Records

The county assessor's office is your first stop. Every property in the U.S. has a record that includes the owner's mailing address. When that mailing address is different from the property address, you've found an absentee owner. Most counties make this data available online for free or for a small fee. You can download CSV files, search by neighborhood, or even filter by zip code. Look for properties where the owner's mailing address is out of state — those landlords are often the most motivated to sell.
2. Paid List Providers and Data Platforms

If you want to skip the manual work, paid list providers like PropStream, BatchLeads, and ListSource let you filter for absentee owners by location, equity percentage, property type, and more. You can stack filters — for example, absentee owners with high equity who haven't refinanced in over 10 years are likely sitting on profit and may be ready to sell. Prices for these services typically run $50 to $150 per month, but even one deal pays for years of subscription costs. For a deeper breakdown of how to use these lists effectively, read our article on [Absentee Owner Lists: How to Find Off-Market Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/absentee-owner-list-deals).
3. Driving for Dollars

Old school still works. Driving through target neighborhoods and looking for signs of neglect — overgrown lawns, boarded windows, peeling paint, mail piling up — often points to absentee-owned or vacant properties. Apps like DealMachine let you photograph a house, pull the owner's contact info on the spot, and add it to a direct mail campaign all from your phone. This strategy works especially well in markets like [Detroit](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/detroit-mi) and [St. Louis](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/st-louis-mo), where aging housing stock and population shifts have left a high concentration of distressed, absentee-owned homes.

Pro Tip: When building your absentee owner list, prioritize owners who have held the property for 10+ years with no mortgage. High equity plus long ownership is a strong signal of a seller who may be ready to cash out — especially if the property shows signs of deferred maintenance.
How to Filter for the Best Absentee Owner Leads

Not all absentee owners are motivated sellers. A property management company that owns 200 rentals is technically an absentee owner, but they're unlikely to sell at a discount. You need to layer filters to find the best leads. Here's what to look for:

items: Out-of-state mailing address — the farther the owner lives, the harder the property is to manage
High equity (50% or more) — gives the owner room to accept a lower offer and still walk away with cash
Long ownership (7+ years) — suggests the owner may be tired of managing the property
Delinquent property taxes — a strong signal of financial stress or disengagement
Single-family homes or small multifamily (2–4 units) — easier to negotiate with individual owners than LLCs
Properties with code violations or liens — public records often available through local municipalities
Vacant properties — combine absentee owner data with vacancy signals for the hottest leads

sections.content: Vacant properties and absentee-owned properties often overlap, and that overlap is where many investors find their best deals. If you want to dig deeper into the vacant property angle, our guide on [How to Find Vacant Properties for Wholesale Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/find-vacant-properties-wholesale) walks through the full process.
How to Reach Absentee Owners: Outreach That Actually Works
Direct Mail

Direct mail is still one of the highest-converting outreach methods for absentee owner leads. A handwritten yellow letter or a simple postcard with a clear message — "I buy houses in any condition, call me" — can get response rates of 1% to 3% on a cold list. That might sound low, but on a list of 500 properties, that's 5 to 15 motivated sellers calling you. Mail the same list every 4 to 6 weeks. Most sellers won't call on the first piece — it often takes 3 to 5 touches before they pick up the phone.
Cold Calling and SMS

Skip tracing your absentee owner list gives you phone numbers to call or text. Services like BatchSkipTracing or Skipforce charge $0.10 to $0.18 per record and return mobile numbers, landlines, and sometimes email addresses. Cold calling works best when you lead with empathy: "I noticed you own a property at 123 Main Street — I work with property owners in the area who are looking for a simple way to sell. Is that something you'd ever consider?" Keep it short, conversational, and low pressure.
Finding Deals Before They Hit the MLS

Absentee owner outreach is fundamentally about getting to sellers before they list with an agent. If you can solve their problem faster and with less hassle than a traditional sale, you win the deal. Read our full breakdown on [How to Find Distressed Properties Before They Hit MLS](https://aiwholesail.com/blog/find-distressed-properties-before-mls) for more advanced strategies that complement absentee owner marketing.
Running the Numbers on Absentee Owner Deals

Once a seller calls back, you need to move fast and make a confident offer. That means knowing your numbers cold. Start with the After Repair Value (ARV) — what the property will be worth after renovations. Then subtract repair costs, your profit margin, and any assignment fee if you're wholesaling. A quick example: a property with a $150,000 ARV, $30,000 in repairs, and a $10,000 wholesale fee should be purchased at no more than $80,000 to $85,000 using the 70% rule ($150,000 x 0.70 = $105,000, minus $30,000 repairs = $75,000 max offer). Use our free [Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to run these numbers in seconds and make sure every offer you submit makes sense before you commit. If you're new to the wholesale side of this business, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide will walk you through the full deal structure.

Pro Tip: Markets with high landlord burnout tend to produce the best absentee owner deals. Cities like [Memphis, TN](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/memphis-tn) have large populations of out-of-state landlords who bought rentals years ago and are now ready to exit. Targeting these high-inventory markets can dramatically increase your deal flow.
Building a Consistent Absentee Owner Deal Pipeline

The investors who win with absentee owner marketing treat it like a system, not a one-time campaign. Pull a fresh list every month, add new records, continue mailing old ones, and track your response rates by list source and mail piece. Over time, you'll learn which filters produce the most motivated sellers in your market. A consistent pipeline means you're always talking to new sellers, and consistency is what separates investors who close 1 deal a year from those who close 1 deal a month.
